text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 3rd in history:
1083 - Henry IV of Germany stormed Rome, capturing St Peter's.
1098 - After a five-month siege in the First Crusade, the Crusaders took Antioch.
1726 - James Hutton, Scottish geologist who wrote the "Theory of the Earth" and was one of the founders of modern geology, born.
1769 - Captain James Cook, a year into his circumnavigation of the world, observed the transit of Venus over the Sun's disc, the main purpose of his voyage.
1808 - Jefferson Davis born. He was President of the Confederate states during the American Civil War. After its conclusion he was imprisoned for two years.
1818 - The last of the Maratha Wars between the British and the Maratha Confederacy in India ended, securing British supremacy in India.
1843 - Frederick VIII, king of Denmark from 1906-12, born.
1853 - Sir William Matthew Flinders Petrie, archaeologist who discovered temples at Giza in Egypt and wrote over 100 books on archaeology, born.
1865 - King George V of England born. He was the second son of Edward VII and ruled from 1910 until his death in 1936.
1875 - French composer Georges Bizet died, the same year his "Carmen" was first produced. It caused a scandal at first but went on to became one of opera's most popular works.
1899 - Johann Strauss Jr, Viennese conductor and composer of waltzes such as "The Blue Danube", died.
1906 - Josephine Baker, naturalised French cabaret singer and dancer who worked with the resistance during the war, born in the U.S.
1911 - Paulette Goddard, U.S. actress and film star, born as Marion Levy. She starred with Charlie Chaplin in "Modern Times" and "The Great Dictator" and was married to him from 1935-42.
1924 - Austrian novelist Franz Kafka died. He wrote "The Trial" and "Metamorphosis" and exerted a huge influence on modern writers.
1925 - Tony Curtis, U.S. film actor who appeared in "Spartacus" and "Some Like it Hot", born as Bernard Schwartz.
1933 - Celso Torrelio Villa, member of the military junta and then President of Bolivia from 1981-82, born.
1937 - The Duke of Windsor, who had abdicated as King Edward VIII of England, married Wallis Simpson in France.
1940 - In World War Two, the evacuation of allied troops from Dunkirk was completed; over 335,000 British, French and Belgian troops were rescued.
1944 - Generals Giraud and de Gaulle reached agreement on the constitution of the French Committee of Liberation under their joint presidency.
1950 - A French expedition reached the top of the Himalayan peak of Annapurna in Nepal for the first time.
1963 - Pope John XVIII, known for his progressive views, died.
1965 - Major Edward White became the first U.S. astronaut to walk in space when he stepped outside his Gemini 4 spacecraft.
1967 - Arthur Ransome, British journalist and writer of children's books such as "Swallows and Amazons", died.
1973 - At the Paris air show the Tupolev 144, a Soviet supersonic airliner, crashed, killing 15 people.
1979 - The worlds's worst oil spillage occurred as a result of a marine blow-out beneath the drilling rig Ixtoc 1 in the Gulf of Mexico.
1982 - Israel's ambassador to London, Shlomo Argov, was shot and seriously wounded.
1986 - Dame Anna Neagle, British actress and dancer, died.
1989 - Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, spiritual leader of Iran, died aged 86.
1990 - Presidents Bush and Gorbachev wound up a superpower summit in the U.S. with agreement on a number of arms control and trade issues.
1992 - The world's largest environmental summit opened in Rio De Janeiro with 178 nations taking part.
1995 - Defence ministers from NATO and European Union countries agreed to set up a "rapid reaction force" to protect embattled U.N. peacekeeping troops from Bosnian Serb aggression.
1996 - NATO foreign ministers backed a path-breaking deal that boosted the role of European members within the Atlantic alliance.
